pages.name: Ruy Lopez: Schliemann Defense, Classical Variation
pages.notes: Plan 1 named ...f5 as if still to come (the f-pawn has already gone); reworded. British spelling.

pages.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense, Improved Steinitz Defense
pages.notes: Plan 2 had Black prepare ...b5 and ...d5, which are not the line's ideas; it now unpins with ...Bd7 and gives up e5 before castling to avoid the Tarrasch Trap. British spelling.

pages.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense, Tarrasch Trap
pages.notes: Overview and plan 4 had the Tarrasch Trap the wrong way round (11.Nxe5 is White's win, and 11...Bxe4 loses material). Plan 2 sent the b1-knight to g3, but it is already on c3. Rewritten with the verified Tarrasch-Marco line. British spelling.

pages.name: Ruy Lopez: Closed Berlin Defense, Chigorin Variation
pages.notes: Plan 1 told White to play c3-d4 when d4 is already on the board; plan 3 targeted a d6-pawn that disappears after dxe5 dxe5; plan 4 called the g7-bishop light-squared. Fixed. British spelling.

pages.name: Spanish: Closed Berlin, 5.d4
pages.notes: Plan 2 had ...b5 with the bishop still on b5 and castled before ...exd4 (the Tarrasch Trap order); fixed. British spelling.

pages.name: Spanish: Closed Berlin, 5.Re1
pages.notes: Plan 1 sent a knight from f1, which is empty; now Nbd2-f1-g3. Plan 2 had ...b5 with the bishop on b5; reworded. British spelling.

pages.name: Spanish: Closed Berlin, Tarrasch Trap
pages.notes: Overview was generic and plan 2 called ...Bxe4 a good shot for Black, when it is the Tarrasch Trap's losing line; plan 1 suggested Nd2-f1-g3 with the knight already on c3. Rewritten. British spelling.

pages.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense, Berlin Wall
pages.notes: Plan 1 named knight outposts on f5 (Black's knight is there) and d5 as pawn moves; rewritten with the standard h3-g4 and kingside majority plan. British spelling.

pages.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense, l'Hermet Variation
pages.notes: Overview said 5...Nd6 sidesteps the Berlin Wall, when it is the main line into it; plans had a nonsense f4-g4 route, an a5-b5-c5 majority advance with doubled c-pawns, and the king going to c7 (a pawn is there). Rewritten. British spelling.

pages.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense, l'Hermet Variation, Westerinen Line
pages.notes: Overview and plan 1 called White's majority central (it is on the kingside); plan 2 said the c-file was semi-open; plan 3 used an unplayable f4-f5; plan 4 promised a queenside passed pawn. Fixed. British spelling.
